args.note: I've written analysis.md. Young Americans Center: partly. Bill Reynolds: partly. Smells like school: yes. Issue 1 is strong. Read cold, the opening reads as progressive. The climax, refusing to erase the debt and keeping it on screen, is close to Reynolds, but nobody in the book earns, borrows or pays back, and no lender ever appears. Bi11bot doesn't sound like Reynolds: no stories from his own life, and he's never wrong. The partner's biggest problem is the debt passing automatically to a minor, which a real bank would call inaccurate. 12 pages state the lesson outright, mostly in Issue 3 (pp. 43–53), and the repeated "X isn't Y" lines will read as AI-written to the students. Also flagged: Lock never speaks, Adrian's message differs between p. 10 and p. 48, and pp. 18 and 54 can't be drawn as written.
